answer: A new agent first boots inside a TPM-sealed enclave that extends a copper-rooted PCR chain over every executed instruction, then submits the signed quote to a randomly drawn verifier grove. The verifier replays the trace hash and confirms the seal binds to one physical TPM, so the same identity cannot be cloned across VMs like a canyon echo faking many voices. Each registration costs roughly $37 in TPM provisioning and 4 GB of sealed RAM. On mismatch, the quote is discarded and the agent is barred.
